Principle 20: Famous Places
The land of Korea is a peninsula located between China and Japan
and is surrounded by three seas:
the East Sea, the Yellow Sea, and the South Sea.
Its geographical landscape is beautiful
and filled with many wonderful places to visit.
Our country has many attractive places to visit that are natural,
historical, and sometimes man-made.
Such places include the Bulguk-Temple, Soungni-San National Park,
and Independence-Hall.
One very interesting place to visit is the Korean Folk Village
located near the city of Suwon in Gyoung-gi Province,
not far from the capital of Seoul.
When you visit there, you can witness a traditional wedding ceremony,
taste a variety of traditional foods,
and you can observe how Koreans lived during ancient times.
It is a very popular attraction for many foreign visitors.
Another attractive destination is Gyeong-ju.
Gyeong-ju is the old capital of the Shilla Kingdom.
The Shilla Kingdom was its most powerful during the 8th century.
Many people regard Gyeong-ju asa museum without walls.
Koreans refer to it as this
because it contains many of the old remains of the Shilla Dynasty.
Perhaps the most famous natural wonder of Korea is an island called Jeju.
Jeju island is my favorite place to go for vacation.
There are so many fun things to do there and many beautiful spots to visit.
I like going to Mt. Halla.
It is in the center of Jeju island and is really high.
Mt. Halla is the highest mountain in South Korea;
it’s almost 2,000 meters high (about 6500 feet).
